To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Weekly Fleet Planning — Pipeline-Linked Sizing & Budget Reconciliations

Team — putting this on the calendar for our weekly fleet planning cycle. Acme just shared a preliminary Q4 consumption forecast (attached) and they want a pilot-sized reservation with the option to convert to a reserved pool by Nov. High-level asks: a short-term guaranteed footprint for the pilot, and a runway plan that lets Sales/Finance sign a committed monthly capacity starting in Oct if we hit their usage milestones.

Quick context: Acme is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a line-of-business ML feature. Their procurement asked for a capacity estimate tied to the pilot and a budgetary projection for conversion. Deal: D-2026-ACME-42.

Please review the attached Acme_Monthly_Forecast.xlsx and the GPU_Sizing_Model_v3.csv. I need three things by EOD Tuesday:
- Karthik: recommended reserved GPU count for an 8-week pilot (expected peak concurrency + safety buffer) and an hourly latency SLO target.
- Laura: budgetary impact and how this would show up in our committed capacity revenue run-rate; also confirm billing cadence if we create a short reserve contract.
- Markus & Vivek: ops/infra runbook for onboarding a reserved pool (provisioning time, expedited allocation options) and any runway constraints for the us-west region.

I'll loop in Marissa and Rishi on negotiation levers once we have sizing. We should treat this as an agenda item in Friday's fleet planning call — I want a clear decision path (pilot size, commit threshold, and fallback policy).

Thanks —
Evelyn Hart
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Acme_Monthly_Forecast.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB), GPU_Sizing_Model_v3.csv (csv, 28KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly Fleet Planning — Pipeline-Linked Sizing & Budget Reconciliations

Evelyn — ran the numbers against the attached sizing model. Quick summary:

- Pilot window: 8 weeks (Sep 1–Oct 26) as proposed.
- Baseline concurrency estimate (from Acme sheet): 120 active sessions at peak.
- Recommended reserved pool: 10 x A100-80GB equiv GPUs with continuous batching and prefix caching enabled. That gives ~150 peak concurrent prompt tracks assuming 8 token/sec average; includes a 20% safety buffer.
- If Acme wants strict p95 latency <= 300ms for short prompts, we should size to 12 GPUs or add a latency-priority burst pool of 2-4 GPUs for peak windows.

Operational notes:
- Provisioning lead time for 10 GPUs in us-west is ~6 business days under current inventory. If we need expedited allocation, we can stand up temporary hot-swap capacity via partner pool (CloudPartner) in 48–72 hours but at a higher unit cost.
- KV cache prewarming reduces effective cost; we should include a one-time cache-warm run for the pilot onboarding.

I can produce a per-day cost table and a sensitivity matrix (concurrency vs GPUs) by tomorrow morning.

— Karthik
VP, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-24T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Weekly Fleet Planning — Pipeline-Linked Sizing & Budget Reconciliations

Adding the finance view. Two things to flag:

1) Revenue recognition & billing cadence: a short pilot reservation (monthly billed) can be treated as committed capacity if we include a minimum spend clause. For quoting purposes, 10 GPUs x pilot term translates to an ARR run-rate delta of approximately $1.2M (annualized) if Acme converts. We should surface this to Sales to set expectations.

2) Credit & discount levers: For an 8-week pilot we can offer a 10–15% placement discount if they commit to a 12-month conversion within 60 days of pilot completion. Any deeper discount would need revenue ops sign-off (Rishi + me).

Request for the fleet call: please bring a worst-case budget (expedited partner allocation) and a baseline budget (native provisioning). I'll prepare line items and a short P&L stub for Friday.

Laura Bennett
Director, Finance — GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: Proposal_D-2026-ACME-42.pdf (budget stub)

Quick ops replies:

- Onboarding runbook: we can provision a dedicated pool and attach the customer tenancy in ~5–7 business days (infra ticket + network ACLs + KMS key binding). I'll drop a short checklist into the drive folder.
- Expedited options: partner hot-pool as mentioned (48–72h) or rebalancing low-util internal pools for a soft-launch (24h) — both carry tradeoffs (cost, telemetry limitations).
- Capacity constraints in us-west: we have two refresh waves planned in late Sep; if Acme defers to Oct commit we get better margin visibility.

I'll be on the fleet call Friday to run through the checklist and estimate ops effort hours.

Markus Klein
Head of Platform Operations

Thanks all. Summary & asks for Friday's call:

1) Karthik: bring the sensitivity matrix (GPUs vs concurrency vs p95 latency) and a per-day cost table for both native and expedited partner allocations.
2) Laura & Rishi: bring the P&L stub and discount guardrails (include the minimum spend language).
3) Markus & Vivek: finalize the provisioning checklist and confirm provisioning SLA under both normal and expedited workflows.

Agenda item: decision nodes — pilot size, commit threshold to convert to reserved pool (usage % / weeks), and default fallback (partner pool vs dynamic rebalancing).

I'll record the call and capture the decision path in the deal record. Procurement @Acme: we'll follow up with a formal pilot statement of work and revised proposal once internal sizing and finance checks are complete.

Thanks —
Evelyn Hart
